extracted.intended_audience: Naval Postgraduate School researchers, US Coast Guard leaders, government contracting officers, and policy analysts interested in OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_description: A master's thesis analysing reasons for post-award cost increases on OMB Circular A-76 contracts for U.S. Coast Guard activities, comparing contract costs to the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO), and assessing USCG perceptions of A-76 implementation and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: DOL wage determinations were identified (in an earlier study of three USCG A-76 contracts) as a cause of post-award cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an explicit factor to explain contract cost increases; the abstract notes that DOL wage determinations contributed to increases even though contracts in the earlier study remained cost effective. Investigate whether DOL wage adjustments alter contractor labor costs relative to the original cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Added work / scope growth after award
rubrics_metrics.description: Added work on contracts was identified as a cause of cost increases in prior analysis and is investigated in the thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat scope changes or additional tasks added post-award as a likely driver of increased contract costs; examine contract modifications and change orders to quantify impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other/additional factors causing cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: The thesis analyzed whether additional factors (beyond DOL wage determinations and added work) caused cost increases on A-76 contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a broad set of potential contributors (unspecified in the abstract) — e.g., inaccurate initial estimates, supervision/administration costs, market changes — and test their association with cost escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of contract costs with the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract costs were compared with the Government's MEO for each activity to determine if Government savings were still being realized after award and subsequent cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MEO cost baselines as the reference point for evaluating whether contracting out produced net savings post-award; include post-award cost changes when making the comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of post-award cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether contracts remained cost effective despite experiencing post-award cost increases (earlier study indicated they were still cost effective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume cost increases eliminate savings — explicitly recalculate cost-effectiveness including wage determinations and added work; document thresholds/metrics used to call a contract 'cost effective.'

rubrics_metrics.name: USCG perceptions of A-76 effectiveness (implementation perceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews were conducted with USCG leaders from units with contracted-out commercial activities and compared to interviews with leaders from units that kept functions in-house to gauge perceptions of A-76 effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perceptions (qualitative data) are used to identify implementation problems and attitudes toward A-76; compare perspectives across units with contracted versus in-house functions to detect systematic differences. Use interview protocols and compare themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation problems associated with perceptions of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract notes there are problems in the implementation of A-76 that may be associated with perceptions of its effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific implementation issues (e.g., communication, transition management, oversight) that correlate with negative perceptions; frame these as possible causes of program resistance or perceived failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer actions to control post-award cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: The study analyzed what the Coast Guard contracting officer could do to control cost increases on A-76 contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate practical mitigation measures available to contracting officers (e.g., tighter specifications, better oversight, contingency planning, clearer solicitation terms); treat recommended actions as prescriptive criteria for improving outcomes.
